summary: The root نكص (nkS) means to recede, retire, or draw back from something, often due to awe or fear. It can also mean to turn back from something one had applied themselves to, especially a good thing.
lane: 1 نَكَصَ عَنِ الأَمْرِ ذ , (A, K,) [aor. نَكِصَ , and sometimes نَكُصَ , as will be shown below,] inf. n. نُكُوصٌ (S, IF, A, Msb, K) and نَكُصٌ (A, K) and مَنْكَصٌ (K) and نَكَصَانٌ , (MA,) He receded, retired, or drew back from the thing, or affair, refrained, forbore, abstained, or desisted, from it; recoiled from it, shrank from it, or drew back from it in awe or fear; (S, IF, A, Msb, K;) as also نَكَثَ عَنْهُ . (Aboo-Turáb, TA.) You say also, نَكَصَ عَلَى عَقِبَيْهِ , (S, Msb, K,) or على عَقِبِهِ , (A,) aor. نَكُصَ (S, Msb) and نَكِصَ , (S,) or the latter only, (Sgh, TA,) or the former is allowable, (Zj, TA,) He turned back from a thing to which he had applied himself; (IDrd, S, * A, * Msb, * K, TA;) meaning a good thing; and sometimes an evil thing; (IDrd, TA;) or meaning particularly a good thing; or extr. with respect to an evil thing. (K.) [See the Kur, xxiii. 68.] Hence [as syn. with نكص ], though we have not heard it. (Mgh.)

headwords.gloss: His lot; portion, is decreasing; deficient, and his good fortune is receding

parts.t: deficient, and his good fortune is receding

headwords.def: حَظُّهُ نَاقِصٌ وَجَدُّهُ نَاكصٌ (tropical:) [ His lot, or portion, is decreasing, or deficient, and his good fortune is receding ]. (A, TA.)

headwords.gloss: A place to which one removes, withdraws; retires afar off; O 'Alkamah, affairs have compelled me to have recourse to thee, and there was not for me any place to which to retire

parts.t: A place to which one removes, withdraws,
. (O, B, K.) El-Aashà says, praising 'Alkamah Ibn-'Olátheh,
O 'Alkamah, affairs have compelled me to have recourse to thee, and there was not for me any place to which to retire.

headwords.def: مَنْكَصٌ , (O, B, K,) like مَقْعَدٌ , (TA,) [in the CK, erroneously, مُنَكَّص ,] A place to which one removes, withdraws, or retires afar off, syn. مُتَنَحًّى . (O, B, K.) El-Aashà says, praising 'Alkamah Ibn-'Olátheh, أَعَلْقَمُ قَدْ جَبَرَتْنِى الأُمُورُ إِلَيْكَ وَمَا كَانَ لِى مَنْكَصُ [ O 'Alkamah, affairs have compelled me to have recourse to thee, and there was not for me any place to which to retire. (TA.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
